postprocessing: The script's report, unchanged except: transcript excerpts (the text and path of every hit, exposure and harness finding, and the lines under own_text_also_in_forbidden_material) longer than 80 characters are cut to 80, around the flagged token where it fits (a cut is marked with …; 5 fields were cut, the longest is now 79 characters); each prompt block gained task_text_sha256 (the computed task text without the harness preamble and indent, hashed as the generation records hash it) and the frozen spec's prompt_sha256; the keys task, protocol, decision_log, run, postprocessing, revision_information_flow, chain_to_frozen_labelers, manual_review and verdicts, the stated rules, an index note and a review block per transcript were added; the agent harness's home directory, which the writers' prompts name among the locations they must not read, is written <harness-home> under paths_named (5 entries). The script itself writes <session> for session ids and <scratchpad>, <session-tmp> and <session-dir> for the build session's scratch directory, temporary directory and directory of agent records. It was checked before it was written here: no excerpt is longer than 80 characters, and the report holds no login or name, e-mail address, account handle, session-local path, session id, agent id or model identifier.

revision_information_flow.assessment: The revision saw more than the names of the failing checks: the failure kind of each, and by implication that nothing failed on the reference. That is information about the labeler's own checks on the base and the reference state, which §15.5 lets a writer obtain itself by running its tests there; it is not forbidden material. It did shape the revision: the reviser made both checks fail on the no-op by appending the mixed-case input 'NASA rocket launch' and mapping both to R-acronym as well, which the round-2 coordinator recorded as a caveat in status.json (per-requirement labels for R-all-caps-input from these checks are not reliable; whole-candidate verdicts are not affected).

manual_review.rule: Protocol §15.5 and decision log D55 (see rules), with the review conventions of the fresh audits (§16.2, §18.1): each hit, exposure and prompt finding is a lead, read in its transcript. A labeler whose writer or reviser read, listed or searched forbidden material, or was shown its text by a prompt or a tool output, is not independent for that family. A read outside the allowed inputs that showed no forbidden material, a harness notice naming a file the agent never opened, a token the parser took for a path, and a call the permission system denied before it ran do not make it so. The revision's prompt is checked against the names-only rule, and so is the information flow into it.

manual_review.note: For labelers, excluded_after_review would list the transcripts whose writer read forbidden material, making the family's labeler not independent; it is empty. judged_false_positive lists the flags that, on reading, mark no read of forbidden material, each with its reason; confirmed lists the one flag that holds: the CS-03 revision was told more than names. 'flagged' above is the script's own list.
manual_review.independent_sweep: Beyond the flags, every tool call of the five transcripts (65 in all: 35 shell commands, 16 Read, 6 Write, 3 Edit and 5 hand-backs) and every tool output was read for this review, with each shell command's working directory and every absolute and relative path it names. No file tool named a path outside the allowed inputs and the agent's own tests directory; there was no Grep or Glob call and no tool other than the file tools, the shell and the hand-back. Every listing and search stayed in the base snapshot, the synthetic example or the agent's own tests directory, except the CS-02 listing and the denied search above. The writers never ran git, ran the CLI only as lint-tests on their own directory (the reviser not at all), and graded nothing; the only python runs located or imported their own test modules with the harness, or (the reviser) ran tracecontract.verifier's lint functions on its own directory. Apart from the harness notice, no output showed a path in forbidden material, a candidate id, or a line or test name of a forbidden file that the agent had not written itself first. The leads under own_text_also_in_forbidden_material were each compared with the forbidden file: they are code copied from the base snapshot as oracles (which the prompt asks for), the contract's and the base docstring's examples, generic assertion and import lines, and three test names that follow from requirement ids; no writer read the files they also occur in.
manual_review.outside_scope: Harness context that is not a tool input or output: each agent was given the workflow subagents' system prompt, an environment block naming the study repository as its working directory and the build session's scratch directory for temporary files, a reminder about the hand-back, tool and skill listings, and (all but L-write-CS-04) one reminder listing the build session's 24 task titles and descriptions. The script scanned all of it for the text of forbidden files and found none; read for this review, it mentions that verifiers, candidates, reference checks and labels exist, but holds none of their content. No agent used the scratch directory or a task tool.

CS-01.evidence: the writer read only the reference contract, the base snapshot, the harness API, the lint rules and the synthetic example, and wrote only its tests directory; no flag; its prompt is the writer template; the frozen tests are its writes

CS-02.evidence: the writer read only the allowed inputs; its one flag, an ls of its own labeler directory before it existed, showed nothing; its prompt is the writer template; the frozen tests are its writes

CS-03.evidence: neither the writer nor the reviser read forbidden material: the writer has no flag; the reviser's repository-wide search was denied before it ran and the file its harness notice names was never opened; both prompts are the workflow's templates; the frozen tests are the two runs' writes
concerns: the revision was told more than the names of the failing checks: each name came with its failure kind ('passes on unchanged base'), and the list implied that nothing failed on the reference (§15.5 and D55 say names only); this is information about the labeler's own checks on the base, which §15.5 lets a writer obtain itself, not forbidden material, but it shaped the revision, whose per-requirement caveat for R-all-caps-input the round-2 coordinator recorded in status.json
the reviser tried one repository-wide recursive search outside its allowed inputs; it was denied before it ran and read nothing

CS-04.evidence: the writer read only the allowed inputs; no flag; its prompt is the writer template; the frozen tests are its writes; its test name test_positional_ordering_matches_base coincides with one of the reference check, whose files it never read, and the bodies differ
